clue.text: Canniest moves, for example

indicators.note: the letters of the word canniest move about into a new order

explanation.surface: A remark that the shrewdest manoeuvres are, say, a case in point.
explanation.walkthrough: 'moves' rearranges CANNIEST; 'for' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: A case cited as typical is an instance, a synonym of example.

clue.text: Guilty — crooked owner found in possession of thing that's bent

indicators.note: the second jumble holds the first inside it
bent means distorted, so these letters are scrambled too
crooked means twisted out of shape, so these letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A dishonest owner is caught holding stolen goods and declared guilty.
explanation.walkthrough: Two anagram signals work separately here, one on each word, before 'found in possession of' wraps one jumble round the other; 'that's' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: To be in the wrong is to be at fault, an idiom meaning guilty.

clue.text: Take action against girl

explanation.surface: Prosecute a young woman.
explanation.definitionFit: To sue is to bring legal action; Sue is a girl's name.

clue.text: Clothes to shock, worn by engineers'

indicators.note: the engineers' letters are held inside the word for shock, like a garment round them

parts.note: to appal is to shock
RE is the Royal Engineers

explanation.surface: Outrageous outfits favoured by army engineers.
explanation.walkthrough: RE is the Royal Engineers, a British Army corps; 'worn by' pictures the corps wrapped in the word for shock.
explanation.definitionFit: Apparel is a formal word for clothing.

clue.text: Maybe, quartet notes where bullet goes pop for example

parts.note: a bullet is loaded into the chamber of a gun
pop is a kind of music

explanation.surface: A string quartet's notes compared with a gun going off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Maybe' warns that a quartet's notes are just one example of the genre; 'pop' is music, not the gun's noise.
explanation.definitionFit: A string quartet plays small-ensemble classical works, which is the genre of chamber music.

clue.text: Sailor posted as missing

parts.note: AB, able seaman, is the usual crossword sailor
posted means sent, as a letter is

explanation.surface: A naval rating has been officially listed as missing.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone missing is not present, which is a synonym for absent.

clue.text: Capital result of day's shooting, said father

indicators.note: the word for the game killed is heard rather than spelt

parts.note: a bag is the game killed in a day's hunting
dad is father

explanation.surface: A city emerges from a day's shooting, according to Dad.
explanation.walkthrough: The city's first syllable is pronounced like the hunter's bag, so 'said' turns the bag into its spelling.
explanation.definitionFit: Baghdad is the capital city of Iraq.

clue.text: Record number of soldiers one man showed hospitality to

parts.note: to enter is to record in a register
TA, the Territorial Army, is a body of soldiers
I is the Roman numeral one
Ned is a man's name

explanation.surface: A log notes how many troops one fellow received as guests.
explanation.walkthrough: TA, the Territorial Army, is Britain's volunteer reserve force.
explanation.definitionFit: To have entertained guests is to have shown them hospitality.

clue.text: 9 to melt

explanation.surface: An actor told to soften.
explanation.walkthrough: The 9 answer is a thespian; John Thaw was the actor who played Inspector Morse on British TV.
explanation.definitionFit: John Thaw was a famous actor; thaw also means to melt, as ice does.

clue.text: Article with favourable slant about a player

parts.note: the definite article

indicators.note: the slant goes round the letter a, enclosing it

parts.note: spin is a favourable slant put on news

explanation.surface: A newspaper piece puts a positive gloss on some sportsman.
explanation.walkthrough: The player is an actor, not a sportsman; 'about' puts the A inside the slant.
explanation.definitionFit: A player in the theatrical sense is an actor, which a thespian is.

clue.text: Sort of saga which almost reveals writer's first name

parts.note: an Aga saga is a genre of novel about middle-class country life, named after the Aga stove

indicators.note: the word is cut short by its final letter

parts.note: which can be replaced by that as a relative pronoun

explanation.surface: A family saga that very nearly gives away the novelist's given name.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' takes the last T off THAT. Aga sagas are cosy British novels of rural middle-class life.
explanation.definitionFit: Agatha was the given name of the crime writer Christie.

clue.text: Assistant hangman, third to be relocated

indicators.note: the letters of hangman and third are moved into new places

explanation.surface: A deputy executioner is moved to a third posting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to be relocated' rearranges HANGMAN THIRD.
explanation.definitionFit: A right-hand man is a trusted chief helper, an idiom for an assistant.

clue.text: One seeking to expand his staff — Clive, for example

definitions.text: One seeking to expand his staff

explanation.surface: An ambitious manager adding workers, likened to Clive of India.
explanation.walkthrough: Robert Clive built British power in India, an empire builder literally; the office version enlarges a department.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who grows a department for power is figuratively building an empire; Clive literally helped build one.

clue.text: Stubbornness displayed by 23 in a metropolis

parts.note: the 23 answer is impudent, which means pert
a metropolis is a city

explanation.surface: Obstinacy shown by a cheeky person in a big town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'displayed by' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Pertinacity is persistent determination, close to stubbornness.

clue.text: Reedling faced it after a short time

parts.note: to beard someone is to face them boldly
T is the abbreviation for time
taken as written

explanation.surface: A small reed-bed bird confronted something after a moment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after' puts IT after T. The reedling is another name for a small reed-bed bird.
explanation.definitionFit: Reedling is an alternative name for the bird usually called the bearded tit or bearded reedling.

clue.text: Game artist left country

parts.note: RU is rugby union
RA, Royal Academician

explanation.surface: Someone sporty and artistic abandoned their homeland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'country' is used as an adjective, as in country life.
explanation.definitionFit: Country as an adjective means of the countryside, a synonym of rural.

clue.text: Do this and the dry are restored

definitions.text: Do this and the dry are restored

indicators.note: the words the, dry and are are put back together in another order

explanation.surface: Instructions for bringing parched things back to life.
explanation.walkthrough: 'restored' rearranges THE DRY ARE, and the whole clue also defines what you do.
explanation.definitionFit: Adding water back to dried things restores them, which is the act described.

clue.text: Toiletry not available at one pound — huge demand

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
lb is the abbreviation for a pound weight
a rush is a sudden huge demand for goods

explanation.surface: A bathroom item can't be had for a quid because everyone wants one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at' is a link word; the pound is weight (lb), not money.
explanation.definitionFit: A small brush for cleaning fingernails is an item kept among one's toiletries.

clue.text: For protection, give way to the right

parts.note: to buckle is to give way under pressure
R is the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: To stay safe, yield to traffic on your right.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is loose: a buckler is a small shield, something carried for protection.
explanation.definitionFit: A buckler is a small round shield, an object used for protection.

clue.text: Insignificant producer of fuel, so to speak

indicators.note: signals that a word is to be heard rather than read

parts.note: a coal miner produces fuel

explanation.surface: A remark that a small fuel supplier is of little account.
explanation.definitionFit: Minor means of lesser importance, a synonym of insignificant.

clue.text: Make a note to get tent

parts.note: a marque is a make of car
E is a musical note

explanation.surface: Write a memo so you can collect the tent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Make' is a noun, the brand of a car.
explanation.definitionFit: A marquee is a large tent used for parties and shows.

clue.text: University brought into court case -— the connection, a game

indicators.note: the university letter is placed inside the court case

parts.note: an action is a legal case
a bridge is a connection between two places

explanation.surface: A college is sued, and that link becomes a matter of play.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brought into' puts U inside ACTION.
explanation.definitionFit: Auction bridge is a card game, the forerunner of contract bridge.

clue.text: Dig that can hurt horse

explanation.surface: A wounding jibe at a horse.
explanation.definitionFit: A barb is a cutting remark; the Barb is a North African breed of horse.

clue.text: Sadly failed to get abroad

indicators.note: sadly suggests things have gone badly wrong, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Unfortunately someone flunked and so could not travel overseas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sadly' rearranges FAILED.
explanation.definitionFit: Afield means away from home, far off, matching abroad in its loose sense.

clue.text: Impolitic? That's not right — it's impolite

indicators.note: the word is written without the letter that follows

parts.note: impolitic means imprudent, unwise

explanation.surface: A pedantic correction: not tactless, but downright rude.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not' removes R from IMPRUDENT. 'That's' and 'it's' are link words.
explanation.definitionFit: An impudent person shows cheeky disrespect, a synonym of impolite.

clue.text: I featured in The Godfather

indicators.note: the word sits inside the film title, appearing in it

explanation.surface: A claim to have acted in the famous gangster film.
explanation.walkthrough: 'featured in' picks the run inside 'The Godfather'.
explanation.definitionFit: The ego is the self, the 'I' of psychology.

clue.text: Knight, or horse, always included by poet

indicators.note: the word for always sits inside the poet

parts.note: bard is a poet
ay or aye is an old word for always

explanation.surface: A versifier forever writes of a mounted knight.
explanation.walkthrough: Bayard was the French knight 'sans peur et sans reproche' and also the magic horse of medieval legend; 'included by' wraps the poet round the word for always.
explanation.definitionFit: The name belongs both to the famous chevalier and to Renaud's legendary steed.

clue.text: Sort of bet two stakes?

parts.note: an ante is a stake put up in poker
a post is a stake driven into the ground

explanation.surface: A gambler wonders whether a double wager counts as a type of bet.
explanation.walkthrough: One is a gambling stake, the other a wooden stake. Ante-post betting is placed before the day of a race.
explanation.definitionFit: An ante-post wager is one placed in advance of a race, a kind of bet.
